content:
**Visual observations:**
- Whole-plant wilting/collapse is the dominant symptom — plants are dramatically drooped and fallen over
- Foliage remains green (no yellowing, no spots), indicating sudden vascular disruption rather than foliar disease
- Multiple plants affected across raised white plastic-mulch beds in a tomato field
- Collapse appears complete and permanent (not partial or one-sided)

**Reasoning through classes:**

- The green wilt (plants still green but totally collapsed) immediately rules out foliar diseases (Early Blight, Late Blight, Septoria, Powdery Mildew, Leaf Mold, etc.) which show leaf lesions first
- No visible fungal structures, spore masses, or white mycelium — rules out Gray Mold, Southern Blight, Sclerotinia, Rhizopus
- No leaf bronzing or ring patterns — rules out TSWV, CMV
- V-shaped lesions not visible — rules out Verticillium Wilt
- Dramatic sudden whole-plant collapse with green foliage on plastic-mulch raised beds strongly points to a soilborne bacterial vascular disease
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt** description matches best: progressive permanent wilt, base rot, vascular discoloration, ultimately plant death — exactly what this field displays. The plastic mulch / warm-climate production context is also consistent
